answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn fees or vote; the contract slashes that bond when an independently verifiable task is fraudulently claimed. Creating a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, and coordinating them risks losing real capital, so fake accounts are costly even when names are cheap. A fable written with an ivory quill may persuade a person, but it cannot recover collateral after a proof-backed slash.
